summary: Markets are risk-off and highly event-driven: oil plunged on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy, while gold rebounded and technology shares remained under pressure ahead of US midterm elections.[1][2] Bitcoin and Ether recovered modestly but remain vulnerable after the Binance hack and large customer withdrawals; no verified same-day analyst calls were available for most requested altcoins.[5]

signals.name: Bitcoin
signals.reason: Bitcoin remains under pressure after the Binance security breach and fell to a six-week low despite a modest rebound.[5]

signals.name: Ethereum
signals.reason: Ether bounced slightly but remains near a two-month trough amid continuing crypto-exchange risk.[5]

signals.name: Solana
signals.reason: No verified same-day source in the available results provided a directional call for Solana.

signals.name: Apple
signals.reason: Apple was reported lower in choppy trading as technology shares remained weak ahead of earnings.[1][7]

signals.name: Nvidia
signals.reason: The technology and AI complex remained shaky after the prior week’s selloff, weighing on large-cap technology sentiment.[1][10]

signals.name: Alphabet
signals.reason: Alphabet was reported to have slipped as technology-sector weakness persisted.[1]

signals.name: Gold
signals.reason: Gold rebounded as much as 2.5% from a one-year low, supported by geopolitical risk and oversold conditions.[2][6]

signals.name: Brent Crude Oil
signals.reason: Brent suffered its biggest one-day fall since April as hopes for US-Iran negotiations reduced perceived supply-disruption risk.[1][2]

signals.name: US Dollar Index
signals.reason: The dollar eased ahead of the US midterm elections as Treasury yields retreated.[5][7]

signals.name: Norwegian Krone
signals.reason: The Norwegian krone was the biggest G10 decliner, falling more than 1% as oil prices collapsed.[1]

signals.name: Swiss Franc
signals.reason: The Swiss franc was the strongest G10 currency as investors favored defensive assets amid market uncertainty.[1]

signals.name: Australian Dollar
signals.reason: Forex Factory listed Australian commodity prices as the day’s scheduled currency-market event, but the available results contained no directional analyst call.[8]

signals.name: BNB
signals.reason: Binance-related contagion risk is elevated after hackers stole roughly $6.3 billion and customers withdrew billions from the exchange.[5][10]

signals.name: WTI Crude Oil
signals.reason: WTI experienced its largest one-day decline in months as diplomacy hopes reduced expectations of prolonged supply disruption.[1]
